experiment: BRANCHFABRIC EXPERIMENT 004 v11 FINAL INTEGRATED GATE
scope: controller PID, worker PID, PGID, SID, and descendant ownership
bounded SIGTERM and explicit SIGKILL fallback
pipe, thread, IPC, resource-tracker, profiler, and zombie detection
Modal launcher rejection of missing, failed, or contradictory cleanup evidence

findings.finding: The Modal wrapper recorded missing or failed cleanup evidence but did not independently reject a contradictory controller success before provisional result publication.
findings.resolution: Added an independent launcher gate that requires the immutable cleanup artifact to equal embedded controller evidence; validates the exact eight lifecycle phases and monotonic ordering; requires empty survivor, profiler, serving, rollout, resource-tracker, zombie, leaked-thread, leaked-IPC, CUDA-process, and cleanup-error sets; binds worker PID/PGID/SID ownership; and requires reaping, pipe closure, IPC release, subreaper restoration, and CUDA release.

findings.finding: A newly owned controller descendant could be missed if Linux reused the PID of a process that was an initial controller descendant.
findings.resolution: Descendant ownership now treats a changed procfs start token as a new identity even when the PID appeared in the initial descendant snapshot; a regression test covers the reuse case.

exact_lifecycle_order.evidence: Controller transition guard rejects insertion, omission, duplication, or reordering; cleanup construction and launcher independently require exact equality.

pid_pgid_sid_and_descendant_ownership.evidence: Worker roots are start_new_session process-group leaders; procfs captures PID/PPID/PGID/SID/start token; ownership follows controller descendants, worker descendants, worker groups, worker sessions, and retained identities. Launcher cross-checks both role roots against owned-child PID/PGID/SID records.

zombie_and_child_reaping.evidence: Popen.poll/waitpid reaps leaders before PGID probes; Linux subreaper adoption enables waitpid of orphaned descendants; surviving Z-state records fail the gate. The dead-leader regression prevents a reaped zombie from being misreported as a live process group.

bounded_signal_escalation.evidence: Both worker groups receive SIGTERM in parallel within a five-second bound, then survivors receive explicitly recorded SIGKILL under the absolute cleanup deadline. Escaped exact-identity helpers receive the same bounded escalation.

pipes_threads_ipc_resource_tracker_and_p.evidence: Worker pipes must be closed; new live controller threads, new /dev/shm entries, surviving multiprocessing resource trackers, and surviving profiler commands independently fail cleanup.

cuda_process_disappearance.evidence: The controller waits under the caller cleanup deadline for the nvidia-smi compute-process inventory to become empty, rechecks stable physical inventory, and rejects CUDA-owning imports in the controller. Launcher requires matching empty controller and cleanup CUDA-process evidence.

forced_kill_reporting.evidence: Every termination action records target PID/PGID, signal, forced flag, target class, and UTC timestamp; forced_kills is the exact SIGKILL subset and does not prevent PASS after verified disappearance and reaping.

launcher_fail_closed.evidence: A provisional successful function result cannot proceed past the controller call unless cleanup evidence is present, PASS-complete, artifact-identical, role-ownership-consistent, and CUDA-empty.

tests.command: PYTHONPATH=python:experiments/branchfabric pytest -q <15 explicit process-lifecycle and launcher-cleanup node IDs>

real_local_forced_group_probe.workload: one process-group leader and one descendant both ignored SIGTERM

limitations: This review did not invoke Modal or any GPU resource.
CUDA process disappearance is verified by fail-closed implementation and unit evidence here; the paid invocation must still produce real in_function_cleanup.json and provider post-return evidence.
